title: Fraction charts of finite coproducts of twists over a graded ring
statement: Let A be any commutative ring with an N-grading 𝒜, r a natural number, and a:Fin r→Z. Let F be the finite coproduct of Proj.twist 𝒜 (a i) [def-weil-pbc-proj-twisting-sheaf]. Over every homogeneous basic open D₊(f) of positive degree, there is an additive injection α from F sections into Away f (Fin r→A). Its range is degreeZeroFractions [def-sc-degree-zero-module-fractions] for the shifted grading: a vector y has degree n when yᵢ lies in 𝒜_(aᵢ+n) if aᵢ+n≥0 and is zero otherwise. The maps α intertwine awayToSection scalars with the canonical homogeneous-localization algebra map. For a canonical restriction with g^e=h*f, e>0 and h homogeneous, a section represented by y/f^m maps to (h^m•y)/g^(e*m). This includes r=0, arbitrary integer shifts, and nilpotent f.

source.place: Lemma 27.8.4 (2),(3), with Definitions 01M6 (3) and 01MN (1); finite-direct-sum consequence of the parent node

proof.text: For any finite family of sheaves of modules, use the coproduct-biproduct isomorphism to define coordinate projections. The sum of the projection-inclusion composites is the identity by biproduct.total. On sections this proves injectivity of the coordinate map, and the sum of the included coordinate sections supplies a preimage of every tuple. This works on every open, including for the empty family.

Take the compatible single-twist fraction charts beta for all integer shifts. Compose the coproduct coordinate projections on D₊(f) with beta in each coordinate. Invert the bijective finite localization coordinate map awayPi to obtain an additive map alpha into Away f (Fin r→A). The proved coordinate identity awayPi(alpha(s))_i=beta_i(projection_i(s)) and injectivity of beta and of the section coordinate map prove injectivity of alpha.

The finite localization theorem characterizes shifted degree-zero vector fractions coordinatewise. Each beta has exactly its shifted degree-zero range, so alpha has image in the required set. Conversely choose a beta-preimage of every coordinate of a vector fraction in that set, combine those sections using surjectivity of the coproduct section coordinate map, and use injectivity of awayPi to show that alpha of the combined section is the original vector fraction.

Apply awayPi to the scalar and restriction formulas, using its injectivity. For scalars, awayPi_smul and linearity of the coproduct projections reduce the formula to scalar compatibility of beta. For restrictions, naturality of each coproduct projection commutes it with restriction, and awayPi_mk projects a vector fraction to its coordinate fraction. The single-twist restriction formula gives the desired equality in every coordinate.

proof_origin.place: Finite coproduct consequence of (2),(3), Definition 01MN (1); G3 Lean assembly via single twist charts, biproduct total identities, and finite localization products

theorem finite_twist_coproduct_fractions
    {A σ : Type v} [CommRing A] [SetLike σ A] [AddSubgroupClass σ A]
    (𝒜 : ℕ → σ) [GradedRing 𝒜] (r : ℕ) (a : Fin r → ℤ) :
  ∃ alpha : ∀ (f : A) (b : ℕ),
    0 < b → f ∈ 𝒜 b →
    (∐ (fun i : Fin r ↦ twist 𝒜 (a i))).val.obj (op (basicOpen 𝒜 f))
      →+ LocalizedModule.Away f (Fin r → A),
  (∀ (f : A) (b : ℕ) (hb : 0 < b)
    (hf : f ∈ 𝒜 b),
    Function.Injective (alpha f b hb hf) ∧
    Set.range (alpha f b hb hf) = degreeZeroFractions
      (fun n : ℕ ↦ (𝒜 n : Set _))
      (fun n : ℕ ↦ {y : Fin r → A | ∀ i,
        if 0 ≤ a i + n then
          y i ∈ 𝒜 (a i + n).toNat
        else y i = 0}) (Submonoid.powers f)) ∧
  (∀ (f : A) (b : ℕ) (hb : 0 < b)
    (hf : f ∈ 𝒜 b)
    (q : HomogeneousLocalization.Away 𝒜 f)
    (s : (∐ (fun i : Fin r ↦ twist 𝒜 (a i))).val.obj (op (basicOpen 𝒜 f))),
    alpha f b hb hf (awayToSection 𝒜 f q
      • s) = algebraMap
        (HomogeneousLocalization.Away 𝒜 f)
        (Localization.Away f) q • alpha f b hb hf s) ∧
  (∀ (f g : A) (b c : ℕ) (hb : 0 < b) (hc : 0 < c)
    (hf : f ∈ 𝒜 b)
    (hg : g ∈ 𝒜 c)
    (inc : basicOpen 𝒜 g ≤
      basicOpen 𝒜 f)
    (e t : ℕ) (h : A),
    0 < e → h ∈ 𝒜 t → g ^ e = h * f →
    ∀ (m : ℕ) (y : Fin r → A)
      (s : (∐ (fun i : Fin r ↦ twist 𝒜 (a i))).val.obj
          (op (basicOpen 𝒜 f))),
      alpha f b hb hf s = mk y (⟨f ^ m, ⟨m, rfl⟩⟩ : Submonoid.powers f) →
      alpha g c hc hg ((∐ (fun i : Fin r ↦
        twist 𝒜 (a i))).val.map
          (homOfLE inc).op s) =
        mk (h ^ m • y) (⟨g ^ (e * m), ⟨e * m, rfl⟩⟩ : Submonoid.powers g))
